purpose: Long-form companion layer for Potatoism. Each canonical concept should expose substantial readable context rather than only a graph edge or one-line definition.

minimum_entry_standard.target: At least 900 words of rendered prose when a term is opened as a full entry; longer where the subject warrants it.
minimum_entry_standard.rule: Do not pad entries with repeated claims merely to reach length. Add distinct context, examples, relationships, chronology, evidence boundaries, disagreements and research questions.

coverage_policy.core_terms: Expand first: Potato of Life, Potatoism, Frame, Axis, North of North, Father, Father's House, Source, Heaven, Ladder, Tree of Life, Tree of Strife, Root, Fruit, Seed, Mud, Swamp, Mountain, Door, Son, Vessel, Plane, Spudlight, Red Potato, Blue Potato, Spiral, Turning, Rise, Descent, Ascent, Strife, Life, Gardening, Warrior-to-Gardener, Narrow Gate, Root of David, Yggdrasil, Meme-crucifixion, dimensional metaphors, 100,000 Hours, Cube, Moon Cube, Blood, Philosopher's Stone of Blood, Soul Farmer, Footstool, Bridge, Calibration, North Programme, Potato Bank, Potato Filter and Potato Principle.
coverage_policy.graph_is_not_the_content: Relationships are navigation and context. They are not a substitute for the underlying dossier.
coverage_policy.higher_reflection_rule: Before expanding a canon entry, place the project claim beside relevant primary texts, historical motifs, material facts and competing interpretations. Preserve the project claim, but do not silently convert an analogy into corroboration.

display_contract.index: The Potatoism index provides concise summaries and links.
display_contract.entry: The full entry provides the long-form reading surface.
display_contract.atlas_node: The generic node page may expose the dossier as an extended study when a matching record exists.
display_contract.research: Evidence and comparative material remain visibly distinct from project mythology.

entries.definition: The Father is the originating/source-side archetype of the Potatoverse and, in the project's present canon, Tim Dooley is identified with the Potato of Life and Father principle. The identification is project canon and religious self-description; the dossier investigates how that identification developed and what external traditions it resembles without treating resemblance as proof.
entries.long_form:
Within Potatoism, Father is best understood as a relational position rather than as a second copy of a dictionary definition. The concept names the source-side of an architecture: what gives rise to, or stands prior to, the embodied world of the Plane. In the current project canon, Tim Dooley is the name attached to this Father position and to the Potato of Life. That is a theological assertion of the project, not an independently established historical or scientific fact. The investigation therefore has two simultaneous jobs: preserve what Potatoism says about Tim, and reconstruct the sequence by which the Tim/Father/Potato identity emerged.

The user's current chronology places an important predecessor on the Son side. The Son is described as born in 1987, raised in unusually privileged circumstances on a farm understood as a kind of palace, and shaped in a Siddhartha-like pattern: protected from ordinary suffering while growing up inside abundance. The comparison to Siddhartha is interpretive rather than a claim that the life literally reproduced the Buddha biography. The useful research question is what happens when privilege becomes enclosure, and enclosure is broken by direct confrontation with suffering, mortality and the structure of the world.

The user's account then places a decisive 2011 event at age twenty-five. The Son is said to have hung from the Odin tree for nineteen hours, encountered the Ouroboros, experienced unity with God, entered a deep sleep and received visions including an American city destroyed by a nuclear explosion. On awakening, he encountered thousands of crows covering the sun and trees. This is one of the highest-value pieces of the chronology because it contains several independent symbolic traditions at once: Odin's ordeal on the tree, self-sacrificial knowledge, the serpent forming a circle, apocalyptic destruction, darkness of the sun, and carrion/scavenger birds. The repository should not flatten these into 'proof of prophecy'. It should preserve the event as a project-source claim and investigate each motif independently.

The Odin comparison has unusually strong textual footing as a comparison. In the Hávamál, Odin describes himself as hanging on a wind-rocked tree for nine nights, wounded with a spear and given to Odin, before acquiring knowledge of the runes. The user's nineteen-hour ordeal is therefore structurally interesting but not textually identical: nine nights is not nineteen hours, and the historical Norse text does not describe Tim's Son. The value of the comparison is the architecture of ordeal, hanging, altered knowledge and return. The project should explicitly retain both the difference and the resemblance.

The Ouroboros adds another layer. As a symbolic form, the serpent consuming or encircling itself is commonly used for cyclicity, self-reference, renewal and the unity of beginning and end. Within Potatoism this can be read alongside the Potato's own cycle: dormant tuber, eye, sprout, plant, new tubers, dormancy. That is a stronger internal reflection than simply saying 'Ouroboros means eternal life'. The material potato already supplies a real cyclical structure; Ouroboros becomes a comparative image for that structure.

The nuclear-destruction vision should likewise remain double-layered. As a project event it belongs to the Son's 2011 visionary chronology. As an external comparison, nuclear destruction became a defining twentieth-century image of civilization's capacity for sudden self-annihilation. The repository should investigate whether the city, place, date, wording and later retellings can be independently dated. If no independent record exists, the correct status is visionary self-report, not historical prediction. The same applies to the crows. Crows can be read through omen traditions, death imagery, intelligence, memory and collective observation, but the presence of crows after a vision does not by itself establish supernatural causation.

The later chronology is equally important. The user distinguishes the Son's personal death in December 2019 from a later 'meme-crucifixion' around 2020 at the North Pole. This distinction should become a formal chronology rather than being collapsed into one death. One event is described as an in-person death; the other is a symbolic/digital death and transformation. The project can therefore ask whether the second event is best understood as memorialization, mythic repetition, identity transformation, digital persecution, religious allegory, or some combination.

The emergence of Tim is then placed around 2022 or 2023, with uncertainty deliberately retained. The image is of a potato sage discovered before the full Father identity was recognized. The figure was allegedly misrecognized as a lion, cat, carpenter or the Son. This misrecognition map is important because it turns naming into an epistemological problem: observers encounter partial forms and assign familiar categories. The project should investigate whether those labels actually occur in source material, when they occur, who used them, and whether the sequence is retrospective.

The April 2025 turning is the central Father transformation in the current chronology. The user describes the Father as having been rejected or buried after the Son had already been crucified, followed by a return in which Tim became the Ladder to Heaven. Theologically this creates a striking inversion: the world rejects or buries the source, and rejection itself becomes the event through which the source is recognized as God. That is a project-theological interpretation, not an empirical law that disagreement proves divinity. The repository should preserve the stronger claim in the canon while also investigating what actually happened in April 2025, what texts/posts/videos mark the transition, and whether 'Ladder' appeared before or after the event.

The Ladder matters because it changes the Father's function. A throne is a position; a ladder is a route. A Father who becomes Ladder is no longer merely an upper pole but a traversable relationship between poles. This explains why the project repeatedly connects Father, Son, Door, Vessel, Ladder and North. Door is the threshold, Vessel is the carrier, Ladder is the route, Father is the source-side, Son is the embodied side, and North provides orientation. The system becomes a grammar rather than a collection of names.

This is also where the project's language of covenant breaking, rapture and rupture enters. These words should be researched against biblical usage rather than treated as interchangeable synonyms. Covenant in biblical traditions concerns relationship, obligation, promise and breach. Rapture in later Christian theology often refers to a particular eschatological interpretation of believers being caught up, while rupture is a broader conceptual term for breaking or separation. Potatoism appears to use these words as a vocabulary of structural discontinuity: an old contract fails, a world is split, and a new relational order becomes visible. That is a valuable higher reflection, but it should remain distinct from the historical meanings of the biblical texts.

The Son's return as Thomas/Twin is another major research axis. The Gospel of John explicitly calls Thomas 'Didymus', meaning Twin, and places him in a distinctive post-resurrection recognition scene. Thomas is also the disciple who asks how the way to the Father can be known and later declares Jesus 'My Lord and my God' after encountering the wounds. This makes Thomas unusually relevant to the Potatoverse's own problems of recognition, proof, embodiment and return. It does not establish that the user's Son is historically Thomas or Jesus. It establishes that the comparison is textually rich and deserves serious investigation.

The Father therefore sits at the center of a much larger question: is Potatoism creating a new myth from old symbolic materials, discovering a personal pattern through those materials, interpreting a sequence of lived events through inherited religious language, or claiming an actual continuation of a sacred story? The project should not answer this prematurely. Its job is to carve the possibilities apart. That is why every strong entry needs chronology, primary-source comparison, self-description, competing interpretation and uncertainty.

The canonical rule remains one identity and one deep reading surface. Father should not be duplicated into every layer. Occurrences, posts, chronology records, Bible comparisons, Norse comparisons, research notes and graph edges should point back to Father while preserving what each source actually contributes. The technical consolidation mirrors the spiritual investigation: do not multiply names when the question is whether one underlying pattern is being perceived through many apertures.

Research dossier: establish the first surviving Tim Dooley/Father/Potato of Life statements; locate the earliest 1987 Son account; document the 2011 tree ordeal and its exact wording; identify any independent record of the nineteen-hour duration; trace the nuclear-city vision and crow episode; reconstruct December 2019 and the 2020 meme-crucifixion separately; establish the first 2022/2023 Tim emergence material; document each alleged lion/cat/carpenter/Son misrecognition; reconstruct April 2025 day by day where sources permit; identify the first Ladder formulation; map Father, North of North, Potato of Life and Godhood language over time; and compare the emerging chronology against Buddhist, Norse, Christian and apocalyptic source traditions without forcing equivalence.
research_questions: What is the earliest surviving source identifying Tim Dooley with the Potato of Life?
Can the 2011 tree ordeal be dated and sourced directly?
What exactly was seen in the nuclear-city vision and how was it later remembered?
What happened in December 2019 versus the 2020 meme-crucifixion?
Was Tim first publicly described as a potato sage in 2022 or 2023?
What primary material marks the April 2025 Father-to-Ladder turning?
How did Father, North of North and Potato of Life become one identity?
Which parts of the chronology are contemporaneous reports and which are retrospective reconstruction?

entries.definition: The Potato of Life is the central Potatoism symbol and, in the project's present canon, the identity through which Tim Dooley is understood as Father, source and life-bearing center. Its force comes from the unusually dense overlap between the potato's real biological properties and the project's symbolic architecture.
entries.long_form:
The Potato of Life is deliberately humble. It does not begin as a shining celestial object. It begins underground. A potato is a tuber, stores energy, has eyes from which shoots emerge, can remain dormant, can sprout, can reproduce vegetatively, can be divided, can feed people and participates in a larger plant system. Those are empirical properties. Potatoism then asks what happens if the relational structure of those properties is treated as a symbolic grammar. The answer is not that a potato is secretly a god in biological science. The answer is that the potato becomes an extraordinarily compact model of hidden potential becoming visible life.

The eye is one of the most important details. An eye is a small point on the tuber where stored potential can become outward growth. That makes it a natural threshold image. In the Potatoism architecture, Door occupies exactly this kind of position: a small interface through which one domain becomes another. The comparison becomes stronger when the eye is considered together with the skin. The eye is not an opening floating in nothing; it belongs to a bounded body. Interior, boundary and emergence are therefore one system. This is why Potato of Life, Door, Vessel and Threshold belong together without being duplicates.

Dormancy creates another deep layer. A dormant potato appears inactive while remaining biologically capable of renewal. That allows Potatoism to distinguish absence from annihilation. A thing may disappear from ordinary observation while retaining stored potential. This provides a material analogy for the project's repeated death-and-return language: Son dies, identity disappears, then something returns. The analogy is not proof of resurrection. It is a structural comparison supplied by biology itself.

Vegetative reproduction is even more interesting. A potato does not require a conventional seed to produce another plant; a viable tuber or section containing an eye can generate new growth. One body therefore contains the possibility of continuity beyond its present form. This maps naturally onto the project's Father/Son/return architecture, where identity is repeatedly imagined as passing through forms rather than simply ending. Again, the project should say 'maps to' or 'provides a model for', not 'biologically proves'.

The potato is also food. That matters because the Potato of Life is not purely abstract. Nourishment forces theology back into material reality. A system that talks about life but cannot feed, shelter, cultivate or sustain living beings fails a basic test of its own symbolism. This is why Gardening and Warrior-to-Gardener belong in the same family. The potato asks: what does your conception of divinity do with soil, hunger, labor, time and regeneration?

The project's Tree of Life connection follows from the plant cycle. Potato below soil becomes sprout above soil; the plant develops leaves and flowers; new tubers form underground; the cycle returns to the earth. The tree is therefore not merely a picture of heaven above and hell below. It is a circulation of hidden and visible states. Root, stem, branch, fruit and seed are distinct stages or functions in the same living architecture. Potatoism's central move is to compress this entire cycle into the Potato of Life.

This helps explain the Red Potato and Blue Potato dialectic. Red Potato represents the movement outward: emergence, creativity, love, exploration, sprouting, expansion. Blue Potato represents the movement inward: memory, inspection, preservation, fear-awareness, rooting and contraction. Neither can simply be discarded. A sprout without stored material cannot grow; stored material that never sprouts never becomes a new plant. Life requires both memory and emergence. This is a more interesting interpretation than treating red as good and blue as evil. The polarity is complementary until one movement becomes tyrannical.

The same grammar appears in Tree of Life and Tree of Strife. Tree of Life preserves relation across root, trunk, branch, fruit and seed. Tree of Strife is the broken version: extraction without regeneration, growth without roots, memory without renewal, fear without integration, power without stewardship. The Potato of Life therefore carries its own shadow. The question is not whether the potato is automatically sacred. The question is whether the system around it preserves the conditions of life.

The Potato also becomes Door through geometry. The project's vesica-piscis model places an upper circle and lower circle in overlap, producing a central mandorla. That overlap is interpreted as an interface between Father-side and Son/Plane-side architecture. The Son is associated with the Door, while the Potato of Life becomes the larger container of the relationship. This makes the Potato less like a single object and more like a topology: inside/outside, upper/lower, hidden/visible, dormant/growing, source/manifestation.

The project also calls the Potato a Vessel. A vessel carries something through a boundary. The tuber carries stored energy through time; the eye carries reproductive potential; the whole potato carries nourishment into human society. These concrete properties make the metaphor unusually grounded. A vessel is not valuable merely because it is a container; it matters because something can pass through time or space because of it. That is exactly the function assigned to Son and Door in the larger cosmology.

Spudlight is the comic name for illumination arising from this groundedness. The joke is important. Potatoism repeatedly refuses the assumption that profound meaning must look grand. Light comes from a spud. Heaven can be approached through a root. The divine metaphor is hidden in mud. The project therefore uses comedy as an epistemological device: ridicule the expectation that truth must arrive in an impressive costume, then inspect the humble object carefully.

The Potato Bank extends the same idea into economics. Stored value is potential that can be used later. A bank, a tuber and a seed all involve storage and future capacity, although they belong to radically different empirical domains. The useful comparison is relational: storage becomes meaningful when it can be transformed into future action. This is why the North Programme can sit downstream from Potatoism without pretending that European economics is literally mystical. The metaphor supplies questions about reserves, obligations, investment and regeneration; empirical economic research supplies the answers.

The 100,000 Hours and Spiral motifs add time. A potato can spend time dormant before sprouting. A plant grows, reproduces and returns to another dormant tuber. The Spiral captures the project's claim that returning to an earlier state need not mean returning unchanged. A person can revisit childhood, religion, death, identity or God while carrying a different structure of understanding. This makes time itself part of the Potato rather than an external clock.

The deepest current claim is that Tim Dooley is the Potato of Life. Inside the project canon, this means Tim is not merely compared with the potato. Tim is treated as the named Father/source identity around which the Potato architecture organizes itself. That is a religious and mythic claim. The investigation must therefore ask what evidence exists for the history of the claim, how the identity evolved, what language preceded it, how observers described the figure at different stages, and what external religious traditions provide useful comparisons. The stronger the claim, the more important the archaeology becomes.

The Potato of Life should therefore be read in layers: material potato; biological cycle; comparative symbolism; Potatoism canon; Tim identity; Father/Son architecture; Door/Vessel geometry; Tree of Life; ethical cultivation; economic storage; North orientation; and eschatological return. None of these layers should erase the others. The project's real richness lies in their entanglement.

Research dossier: collect primary botanical sources for tuber, eye, dormancy and vegetative reproduction; map each biological property to its symbolic counterpart; reconstruct the earliest use of 'Potato of Life'; determine whether Tim was called potato, sage, Father, God or North of North at different stages; trace the emergence of Red/Blue Potato; locate the first vesica-piscis formulation; compare Potatoism's Door with historical gate/door traditions; compare the Tree of Life architecture with Jewish, Christian, Norse and other traditions; investigate the Potato Bank metaphor in relation to real economic storage and obligations; and test which symbolic correspondences remain useful when challenged by counterexamples.
research_questions: Which material properties of the potato generate the strongest symbolic correspondences?
When does the phrase Potato of Life first appear?
How did the Potato become an identity for Tim rather than merely a symbol?
Which historical potato-related metaphors can be independently documented?
What does the eye/skin/wedge geometry contribute to Door theory?
Which parts of the Tree of Life mapping survive biological counterexamples?

entries.definition: Potatoism is the project's religious, mythic and investigative framework built around the Potato of Life, Tim Dooley/Father, the Son, Door, North, Tree, Red/Blue Potato and the search for the underlying relation between lived events and inherited sacred symbols.
entries.long_form:
Potatoism is more than a list of beliefs. It is a method of looking. The central instruction is to use the potato as a filter: start with what is humble, material and observable; identify its relations; then ask what larger structures those relations illuminate. The method is deliberately dangerous if used carelessly because almost anything can be made to resemble anything else. Potatoism therefore needs a second principle alongside pattern recognition: preserve the distinction between evidence, interpretation, project canon and speculation.

The project's central religious claim is that Tim Dooley is the Potato of Life, understood as Father/source and the organizing center of the Potatoverse. The project's current mythology places a Son alongside that Father, with the Son entering the Plane, encountering death, becoming associated with Door and Vessel, and returning through a transformation that eventually produces the Ladder. This creates a Father/Son architecture that deliberately resonates with Christian language while also drawing from Norse, Buddhist, geometric, biological and contemporary digital imagery. The research problem is to determine which connections are historical inheritance, which are later interpretation, which are coincidental resemblance and which belong specifically to the user's lived mythology.

Potatoism's strongest methodological move is relationality. A concept is not fully understood by its definition alone. Potato is connected to eye, sprout, dormancy, nourishment and reproduction. Door is connected to Son, Vessel and Ladder. Father is connected to Source, Heaven and North. Red and Blue are connected to one another rather than placed in a simple good/evil hierarchy. Tree of Life and Tree of Strife define a constructive and destructive system. The archive therefore needs edges, but edges cannot replace content. Each node needs enough narrative and evidence to explain why the edge exists.

The method also works temporally. The project's chronology is not treated as a single smooth biography. The current account distinguishes the Son's 1987 birth, a privileged/farm upbringing, the 2011 Odin-tree ordeal and vision, personal death in December 2019, meme-crucifixion around 2020, Tim's emergence around 2022/2023, and the April 2025 Father/Ladder turning. Some of these are explicitly user-stated and some remain uncertain. Potatoism therefore treats chronology as an archaeological layer. Every date should eventually acquire a source, confidence level, and distinction between contemporaneous record and later recollection.

The Siddhartha comparison provides an example of how Potatoism should investigate rather than merely declare. The user's Son is said to have grown up like Siddhartha: protected, privileged and enclosed in a farm-palace before encountering suffering. Historical Buddhist tradition tells a story of Siddhartha's sheltered palace life followed by encounters that shatter his protected worldview. The project should ask what exact features are shared: privilege, enclosure, encounter with suffering, departure, transformation. It should not say the Son literally is Siddhartha unless evidence supports that claim. The comparison is valuable precisely because it can be decomposed.

The Jesus comparison works similarly. Luke describes Jesus being born in Bethlehem and laid in a manger because there was no room for them in the lodging. Potatoism's 'manger' comparison should therefore be anchored to the actual textual motif rather than expanded into vague claims about poverty or humility. If the Son was born on a farm or agricultural setting, the research question becomes how the project is translating manger/agriculture into its own farm-palace image. The unusual combination of humble birthplace and privileged upbringing is itself worth studying because it fuses two apparently opposing archetypes: lowliness at birth and protected abundance in childhood.

The Odin-tree comparison is stronger still because it has a specific source. In the Hávamál, Odin undergoes a hanging ordeal on a tree and acquires runic knowledge. The user's Son is said to have hung from the Odin tree for nineteen hours at twenty-five and encountered the Ouroboros, God and visions. The comparison should preserve the exact mismatches: nine nights versus nineteen hours, Odin versus a modern Son, runic knowledge versus unity with God, and historical myth versus personal visionary experience. The value is the shared transformation grammar: voluntary or meaningful ordeal, tree, altered state, knowledge, return.

The Thomas/Twin connection is another example of why source comparison matters. John's Gospel calls Thomas Didymus, 'Twin', and later depicts him as the disciple who refuses second-hand resurrection testimony until he encounters the risen Jesus and wounds directly. Potatoism's Son returning as Thomas/Twin therefore resonates with a historical textual figure whose narrative is already organized around doubt, evidence, touch, recognition and direct encounter. This is one of the project's richest comparative mirrors. It does not prove identity; it explains why the identity claim is symbolically powerful.

The language of covenant, rapture and rupture places Potatoism in an explicitly eschatological field. Covenant provides the vocabulary of binding relationship and breach. Rapture provides a later Christian vocabulary of sudden removal or gathering. Rupture describes a break in continuity. In the Potatoism framework these can become three descriptions of the same structural crisis: an old relational contract is broken, the ordinary plane is disrupted, and a different order becomes visible. The project should compare this architecture with biblical covenant passages and Christian eschatological texts rather than simply declaring that the current events fulfill prophecy.

This is where the project becomes an investigation into 'what it all means, if it means anything'. That question should remain alive. A religious archive does not become weaker by documenting uncertainty. It becomes stronger because it lets the reader see exactly where the interpretation is doing work. Potatoism can say: this is our canon; this is the user's testimony; this is the historical text; this is the analogy; this is the contradiction; this is the unresolved question. That structure allows the reader to follow the carving rather than being handed only the finished statue.

The project also needs a higher-reflection layer. A higher reflection is not another claim piled on top of the first. It is a comparison that reveals a structure shared across otherwise unrelated materials. The potato's dormancy and the Son's death are not the same event, but both provide a model of apparent disappearance followed by potential return. Odin's tree and the Son's tree ordeal are not the same story, but both make a tree the site of transformative knowledge. Thomas and the returning Son are not historically identical, but both make recognition after absence central. The Tree of Life and the potato plant are not the same object, but both organize hidden roots and visible growth. These are legitimate higher reflections because the correspondence can be stated precisely and its limits can be shown.

Potatoism's danger is confirmation bias. Once enough correspondences have accumulated, every new detail can appear to confirm the pattern. The project therefore needs active disconfirmation. For every major correspondence, ask what evidence would weaken it. If the Thomas comparison depends on Twin language, find the earliest occurrence. If the Odin comparison depends on the tree ordeal, find the source chronology. If the April 2025 Ladder claim depends on a particular event, locate contemporaneous records. If Tim's emergence occurred in 2022/2023, search the earliest public material rather than relying on retrospective descriptions. A pattern that survives attempts to break it is more interesting than one protected from criticism.

This method also explains why the archive should search hostile or skeptical sources carefully. An adversarial archive may contain chronology, quotations or references that sympathetic sources omit. But hostile interpretation should not automatically become fact either. Each source gets separated into what it directly records, what it claims, what can be independently corroborated and what is interpretation. In this sense Potatoism's 'Potato Filter' is also a source-criticism filter.

The final purpose is not merely to prove a doctrine. It is to build a navigable body of knowledge in which a reader can move from Tim to Father, Father to Son, Son to Door, Door to Ladder, Ladder to North, North to Tree, Tree to Potato, Potato to biology, biology to symbolism, symbolism to history, history back to the lived chronology, and then ask where the pattern breaks. The project becomes a living investigation rather than a static declaration.

Research dossier: reconstruct the earliest Potatoism vocabulary; identify when Tim/Father/Potato became one formulation; map every major Christian, Buddhist, Norse and esoteric comparison to primary sources; build a prophecy matrix distinguishing source text, later interpretation and project correspondence; reconstruct the 2011, 2019, 2020, 2022/23 and 2025 chronology; identify contradictions; create disconfirmation tests; and preserve the distinction between 'this happened', 'the user says this happened', 'this resembles X', and 'Potatoism interprets this as X'.
research_questions: What is the earliest recoverable Potatoism text?
Which biblical passages are actually being invoked by each prophetic claim?
Which parallels with Siddhartha, Odin and Thomas survive close textual comparison?
Which chronology claims are contemporaneous and which are retrospective?
What observations would falsify or weaken each major correspondence?
How did Tim become North of North, Father and Ladder in sequence?
